data.name: Temple of Aluxes
data.detailed_description:
Have you ever wanted to explore a lost temple? This is your chance.
Find the treasures and escape the Temple of Aluxes by solving various puzzles and challenges.

Navigate through the old temple and face a variety of challenges. Look everywhere and leave no stone unturned.
Interact with your surroundings by examining objects to find what you need to get out.
Use your scanner to scan the environment for clues. Can you find all the treasures and solve the puzzles to get out?

Features:

  • A variety of challenging puzzles with varying difficulty.
  • Test yourself in both logic puzzles and skill-based challenges.
  • Large play area with several rooms to explore.
  • Hand scanner to find clues.
  • Immersive environment.
  • Room-scale support.
  • Teleportation support.
  • Full locomotion support

Available for Arcades on SpringboardVR

reviews.review:
Temple of Aluxes is a VR-focused adventure and puzzle game developed and published by Silver Machine Studios. Released in 2017, it takes a simple but fitting concept for virtual reality and builds an entire experience around it: entering a mysterious ancient temple, searching for valuable treasures, solving puzzles, and eventually discovering a means of escape. Instead of attempting to deliver a complicated narrative or combat-heavy campaign, the game concentrates on environmental interaction and exploration, making the temple itself the centerpiece of the adventure.

The basic gameplay revolves around carefully investigating the temple and understanding how its various objects and mechanisms relate to one another. Players are encouraged to examine their surroundings thoroughly because potentially important clues can be hidden throughout the environment. Objects can be inspected and manipulated as part of the process of determining how to proceed. This approach works particularly well in virtual reality, where physically looking around a room and interacting with objects can feel considerably more natural than simply selecting everything with a mouse cursor. The result resembles a virtual escape room combined with a treasure-hunting expedition.

Puzzle variety is one of the more important elements of Temple of Aluxes. Silver Machine Studios incorporates challenges of different difficulty levels while mixing logical problems with skill-based tasks. Logic puzzles emphasize observation and reasoning, requiring players to understand clues and determine how different pieces of the environment fit together. Skill challenges introduce a more physical component that takes advantage of VR controllers. Combining these styles helps prevent the adventure from becoming nothing more than a succession of locks, switches, and simple item-placement exercises.

Another notable feature is the hand scanner, which can be used to investigate the environment for clues. It provides players with an additional method of examining the temple and fits naturally into the archaeological exploration theme. Rather than making every solution immediately visible, the game expects players to investigate their surroundings and recognize when the scanner might reveal useful information. It contributes to the feeling of being an explorer equipped with a specialized tool rather than simply a player moving from one puzzle trigger to another.

The temple contains several rooms, giving players a reasonably broad environment to investigate instead of restricting the experience to a single puzzle chamber. Moving between rooms also creates a stronger sense of progression. Exploring deeper into the structure, finding treasures, and unlocking solutions can provide satisfaction even without an elaborate storyline. The treasure-hunting component additionally gives players a reason to inspect areas beyond whatever is immediately required to reach the exit. The game repeatedly emphasizes careful observation, so players who enjoy searching every corner of an environment are likely to get considerably more from the experience.

Immersion is clearly one of the game's priorities, and its movement options help accommodate different VR preferences. Temple of Aluxes supports room-scale play, teleportation, and full locomotion. Teleportation is useful for players who are uncomfortable with continuous artificial movement, while full locomotion provides a more conventional method of exploring for experienced VR users. Room-scale functionality complements the physical nature of interacting with objects and examining the environment. These options make the temple easier to approach according to individual comfort levels, although VR hardware remains mandatory because this is specifically a VR-only experience.

The game's visual concept benefits from its ancient-temple setting. Mysterious chambers, concealed mechanisms, treasure, and environmental clues are naturally compatible with puzzle design. The atmosphere does not need an extensive narrative explanation to establish the player's objective. Entering an unknown temple immediately creates curiosity about what might be hidden inside, and every newly accessed room potentially contains another mystery. The straightforward premise consequently works in the game's favor, allowing the environmental design and puzzles to carry most of the experience.

There are nevertheless limitations associated with such a concentrated design. Temple of Aluxes is primarily intended for people who enjoy exploration and puzzles, so anyone expecting substantial combat, character development, RPG progression, or a lengthy cinematic narrative may find it too narrow. Puzzle games also tend to lose some replay value once their solutions have been discovered. The thrill comes largely from encountering an unfamiliar problem, examining the available evidence, experimenting with possible solutions, and eventually understanding what needs to be done. Returning after memorizing those solutions cannot completely recreate that initial experience.

Its technical demands are relatively modest for a PC VR game of its era. The listed minimum specifications include Windows 10, an Intel i5-4590 equivalent or better, 4 GB of memory, a GTX 970 equivalent or better, and 3 GB of available storage. SteamVR is required, with standing and room-scale configurations supported. The game is also presented as a single-player experience, reinforcing its identity as a solitary expedition where progress depends entirely on the player's observational and problem-solving abilities.

Temple of Aluxes ultimately works best when viewed as a focused VR escape-room adventure rather than a large-scale action game. Silver Machine Studios uses virtual reality for purposes that make sense for the genre, particularly physical investigation, environmental observation, scanning, exploration, and puzzle interaction. The inclusion of multiple rooms, treasure hunting, logic challenges, skill-based activities, and several locomotion methods gives the experience more variety than its straightforward premise initially suggests.

While its limited scope and naturally reduced replayability keep it from becoming a particularly deep adventure, Temple of Aluxes offers an appealing concept for players who enjoy investigating mysterious locations at their own pace. Its greatest strength is the directness of its design: explore an ancient temple, inspect everything carefully, uncover clues, find its treasures, overcome its challenges, and escape. For VR players interested in environmental puzzles and virtual escape rooms, it provides an enjoyable and appropriately immersive archaeological diversion.

Rating: 7/10
